card: This PR adds an AssertUnreachable macro to util/check.h and mechanically replaces assert(false) and Assert(false) throughout the codebase, backed by a new linter. The change resolves compiler return-type warnings under GCC and clang-cl without relying on C++23 std::unreachable, which would introduce undefined behavior if hit. Importance rests on compiler warning cleanliness across toolchains and preventing unsafe std::unreachable adoption. It has no dependencies.
changed_since_previous: Consensus files like src/script/interpreter.cpp and subtrees are now excluded from the scripted diff to avoid linkage issues, and dead code cleanup following unreachable assertions was separated into its own commit.
evidence: PR description provides a Compiler Explorer reproduction showing GCC and clang-cl warnings when using assert(false) and Assert(false) in non-void functions.
problem: Assertions with falsy literals like assert(false) create ambiguity over NDEBUG semantics and cause clang-cl warnings, while Assert(false) obscures the noreturn attribute behind a function call and triggers GCC return-type warnings. In addition, developers moving towards C++23 may reach for std::unreachable(), which invokes undefined behavior rather than failing cleanly.

risk.why: A mistake in dead-code removal or replacing an assertion that could actually be reached at runtime would crash node processes in sensitive validation or wallet paths.

scope_notes: Includes a scripted-diff commit spanning dozens of files that substitutes falsy asserts with AssertUnreachable and adds util/check.h includes; consensus interpreter files and third-party subtrees are explicitly excluded.
summary: Introduces an AssertUnreachable() macro in util/check.h that directly invokes the noreturn internal_abort_helper. Replaces assert(false), Assert(false), and std::abort() calls across the codebase using a scripted diff, cleans up resulting dead return statements, and adds a linter enforcing the new macro over falsy assertion arguments.
